title: Primitive state is tracked on two independent axes: a per-primitive Global Activation Status and a per-Instance status
content:
Launch Agent 7's Artifact carries a Global Activation Status per primitive, and its observed values differ by primitive: Agent Creation is `Completed` (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.1.1.1), Prime Transformation is `Completed` (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.2.1.1), Executor Transformation is `Inactive` (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.3.1.1), and Agent Token is `Active` (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.4.1.1).

Separately, Instances of any primitive are filed by their own status — `Active`, `Completed`, or `Suspended` — and Invocations can independently be `Failed` (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.1.1.5.1.1).

The two axes answer different questions. Global Activation Status says whether this *primitive* is a live part of the Agent's machinery; Instance status says what happened to a particular use of it. Decoupling them lets the Artifact express states that a single flag could not — for example a primitive that is permanently `Completed` yet retains a Completed Instance holding the configuration that still governs the Agent (the Agent Creation Primitive's Single Instance Configuration Document, A.6.1.1.8.2.1.1.3.1).

It also distinguishes `Inactive` from `Completed`: an unused capability versus a discharged one. That distinction is what makes the Executor path readable as never-taken rather than finished.
description: Observed global values are Completed, Active and Inactive; Instances are separately Active, Completed or Suspended, and Invocations can be Failed
